chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who accused his wife, then left and returned after she had died, he said: "He is given a choice between two options. It is said to him: If you wish, you may hold yourself guilty, then the ḥadd will be carried out upon you and you will be given the inheritance. And if you wish, you may affirm your claim, then you perform liʿān with her nearest relative to her, and there is no inheritance for you."

key_terms.الذَّنْبَ: the liability or blame he bears
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثَ: the inheritance due from the deceased
key_terms.فَلَاعَنْتَ: you perform liʿān, the mutual cursing procedure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man accuses his wife of adultery and she dies before liʿan is completed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a husband who accused his wife of adultery and then returned after her death. He is given a choice either to accept liability for false accusation and receive inheritance, or to proceed with liʿan through her nearest relative, in which case he loses any right to inherit from her.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4856 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali (as)

regarding a man who accused his wife of adultery and then left, only to return and find that she had passed away.
Zayd (as) said: "He is given a choice between two options.
It is said to him: 'If you wish, you can accept the blame upon yourself, in which case the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) will be carried out on you, and you will be entitled to her inheritance. However, if you choose to admit to your accusation, you must perform liʿan (mutual cursing) with her closest living relative, and in that case, you will not inherit from her.'"
